why: The brief's mutation 3: a status prefix without a valid date is no longer recognised as a status, so `**Status: shipped.**` would show as the row's title instead of failing loudly.
A failed read logs the error's whole text, which could carry what GitHub sent; the log must name the error only.
The parser collects rows in reverse, so the ranks no longer follow the file's order.
The page never asks for the backlog, so /triage shows only its loading line.
Round 1, major: the triage load stops naming the backlog's source, so production shows no section while the page tests, which pass the prop by hand, stay green.
Round 1, major: a status prefix is recognised only in its exact case, so `**status 2026-11-11: …**` shows as the title instead of failing loudly.
Rounds 2 and 3, major: only a few characters are allowed between the word and the date, so `**Status    2026-11-20: …**` or `**Status (2026-…)**` shows as the title.
Round 3, minor folded with the major's fix: a struck-through or italic status is not recognised, so `**~~Status 2026-11-19: …~~**` shows as the title.
